from_quote: I find myself complimented with an Address in your last Paper. Whether the Landholder of the Connecticut Courant, and of the Maryland Journal,
rationale: The letter answers the Landholder's "Address in your last Paper", which it attributes to "the Landholder ... of the Maryland Journal"; Landholder No. X, addressed to Luther Martin, appeared in the Maryland Journal of February 29, 1788, a week before this letter.

from_quote: until the Constitution had received its present form, no man was more plausible and conciliating on every subject than Mr. Gerry
rationale: The letter tells the Landholder to "turn to his eighth number, addressed to the Honourable Mr. Gerry" and quotes this passage from it; Martin's quotation differs slightly in wording ("sitting" for "setting", "on" for "upon").
to_quote: until the constitution had received its present form, no man was more plausible and conciliating upon every subject than Mr. Gerry

from_quote: objections different from any thing his letter to the legislature of his State contains, so that if my representation is true, his must be false
rationale: The letter quotes, in quotation marks and with the pronouns shifted, the Landholder's charge in the address to Martin that Martin had put into Gerry's mouth objections different from his letter to the legislature.
to_quote: objections different from anything it contains, so that if your representation be true, his must be false
